decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 9-1. Dissenting: Esther L. George.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in July suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June suggests that economic activity expanded at a modest pace during the first half of the …”

changes.quote: Some indicators of labor market conditions have shown further improvement in recent months, but the unemployment rate remains elevated.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Labor market conditions have shown further improvement in recent months, on balance, but the unemployment rate remains elevated.”

changes.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment advanced, and the housing sector has been strengthening, but mortgage rates have risen further and fiscal policy is restraining economic growth.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending and business fixed investment advanced, and the housing sector has been strengthening, but mortgage rates have risen somewhat and fiscal poli…”

changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Partly reflecting transitory influences, inflation has been running below the Committee's longer-run objective, but longer-term inflation expectations have rema…”

changes.quote: The Committee sees the downside risks to the outlook for the economy and the labor market as having diminished, on net, since last fall, but the tightening of financial conditions observed in recent months, if sustained, could slow the pace of improvement in the economy and labor market.

changes.quote: Taking into account the extent of federal fiscal retrenchment, the Committee sees the improvement in economic activity and labor market conditions since it began its asset purchase program a year ago as consistent with growing underlying strength in the broader economy.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: In particular, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and currently anticipates that this exceptionally low range for the federal funds rate will be appropriate at least as long as the unemployment rate remains above 6-1/2 percent, inflation between one and two years ahead is projected to be no more than a half percentage point above the Committee's 2 percent longer-run goal, and longer-term inflation expectations continue to be well anchored.

The Committee sees the downside risks to the outlook for the economy and the labor market as having diminished, on net, since last fall, but the tightening of financial conditions observed in recent months, if sustained, could slow the pace of improvement in the economy and labor market.

Taken together, these actions should maintain downward pressure on longer-term interest rates, support mortgage markets, and help to make broader financial conditions more accommodative, which in turn should promote a stronger economic recovery and help to ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with the Committee's dual mandate.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.95% APR costs about $49.79 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.69% and moved -17 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.57% would fall by about $30.28 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 7.2%, and employers added an average of 183k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.5% over the past year (August 2013); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.5%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -5 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.04% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 80%, cut 19%, hike 1%.
